news.text: 2 June saw **The Honky Tonk Man** pull off a seismic upset by pinning Ricky "The Dragon" Steamboat in Buffalo, New York, to claim the WWF **Intercontinental Heavyweight Championship**. Clinging desperately to the bottom ropes for illegal leverage during an inside cradle, the Elvis-impersonating heel kicked off what would become an unprecedented 454-day championship reign. Wrestling purists were horrified that one of the finest technicians in ring history had lost the gold to a man whose primary offensive weapon was an acoustic guitar.
news.youtube: Honky Tonk Man wins Intercontinental Championship 1987

news.text: 11 June saw **Margaret Thatcher** guide the Conservative Party to a historic third successive general election triumph, securing a commanding 102-seat majority in the House of Commons. Campaigning on a platform of economic prosperity and trade union reform, the Prime Minister comfortably saw off challenges from Neil Kinnock's revitalised Labour Party and the SDP-Liberal Alliance. Political commentators noted that the Iron Lady had matched a feat of electoral dominance unseen in British politics since Lord Liverpool in the 1820s.
news.youtube: 1987 UK General Election BBC news report Margaret Thatcher

news.text: 12 June saw John McTiernan's sci-fi action thriller *Predator* unleash itself upon North American cinemas, delivering a masterclass in muscular jungle survival. Starring **Arnold Schwarzenegger** as elite commando leader Major "Dutch" Schaefer opposite a camouflage-cloaked alien trophy hunter, the film expertly shifted gears from gung-ho military machismo to relentless claustrophobic suspense. Audiences cheered wildly as Dutch abandoned his heavy weaponry to smear himself in river mud and face the beast in primal hand-to-hand combat.
news.youtube: Predator 1987 original theatrical trailer Arnold Schwarzenegger

news.text: 12 June saw US President **Ronald Reagan** stand before the historic Brandenburg Gate in West Berlin and issue an audacious Cold War challenge to Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev. Speaking within sight of the imposing concrete barrier, Reagan urged the General Secretary to demonstrate genuine commitment to reform with the unforgettable demand: "Mr. Gorbachev, **tear down this wall!**" Soviet state media promptly dismissed the speech as theatrical provocation, entirely unaware the wall would be in ruins within thirty months.
news.youtube: Ronald Reagan tear down this wall speech 1987 Berlin

news.text: 14 June saw novelty pop outfit **The Firm** ascend to the top of the UK singles chart with their maddeningly catchy novelty tribute *Star Trekkin'*. Created on an acoustic shoe-string and driven by a crude claymation promotional video, the song playfully mocked Captain Kirk, Mr. Spock and Scotty with infectious chants of "there's Klingons on the starboard bow". Serious science-fiction enthusiasts winced in collective agony, while school playgrounds across the country ensured the tune became unavoidable for months.
news.youtube: The Firm Star Trekkin official video 1987

news.text: 19 June saw Palace Software's brutal sword-fighting combat title *Barbarian: The Ultimate Warrior* claim the top spot on the UK Gallup software charts across the **Commodore 64** and **ZX Spectrum**. Delivering visceral one-on-one gladiator duels and a notorious spinning decapitation manoeuvre, the game generated massive tabloid controversy thanks to promotional posters featuring model **Maria Whittaker**. Moral guardians complained furiously about the marketing campaign, ensuring teenage microcomputer enthusiasts sprinted to software shops in droves.
news.youtube: Barbarian The Ultimate Warrior C64 gameplay Palace Software

news.text: 29 June saw the royal world premiere of *The Living Daylights* at the Odeon Leicester Square in London, introducing **Timothy Dalton** as a leaner, darker James Bond 007. Attended by the Prince and Princess of Wales, the fifteenth instalment in the spy saga marked a deliberate break from Roger Moore's lighter touch, grounding Bond in dangerous Cold War intrigue and authentic stunts. Fans lauded Dalton's fierce intensity, even if traditionalists mourned the absence of flying cars and double entendres.

gaming.title: Barbarian: The Ultimate Warrior
gaming.reviewQuote: Fluid animation, savage combat, and that unforgettable decapitation move make this an instant classic.
gaming.headline: Swordplay, Decapitations, and Tabloid Outrage
gaming.gameplay: Designed and animated by Steve Brown—who practised with wooden broadswords in his back garden—*Barbarian: The Ultimate Warrior* pitted two muscular swordsmen in bloody arena combat to rescue Princess Mariana from the evil sorcerer Drax. The game introduced a devastating **flying neck chop**: land the strike cleanly, and your opponent was instantly beheaded while a grinning green goblin jogged into the arena to boot the severed head off-screen like a football.
gaming.reception: The game became an overnight sensation in June 1987, propelled in part by an audacious publicity campaign featuring page-three glamour model Maria Whittaker and gladiator bodybuilder Michael Van Wijk. Moral campaigner Mary Whitehouse and religious groups called for outright bans, which only fuelled sales. Gaming critics were genuinely impressed by the combat engine: *Zzap!64* awarded it 87% (Sizzler), praising its fluid multi-frame animation, while *Crash* awarded it 89%.
gaming.impact: *Barbarian* was Palace Software's biggest commercial hit, shifting over 500,000 copies across Europe and proving that controversial marketing paired with tight mechanics could create a cultural lightning rod. Its fluid martial arts animations and instant-kill move helped pave the way for visceral fighting games like *Mortal Kombat* years later.
gaming.youtube: Barbarian The Ultimate Warrior C64 gameplay
